title: spec: Rule 255 next-header chain walk — 'IPv6 extension header' set ambiguous vs implemented TLV-only walk
description: Found by codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-ilye.6 (edge-case pass, performed by worker after reviewer-model timeouts). spec/03-adaptation.md:~419 says the Rule 255 structural walk 'terminates at the first header that is not an IPv6 extension header'. Under RFC 8200 the extension-header set includes AH (51) and ESP (50); but the reference implementation walks only the TLV extension headers {Hop-by-Hop 0, Routing 43, Dest Options 60} (python/src/lichen/ipv6/packet.py:238 _TLV_EXT_HEADERS), treats AH as upper-layer opaque payload, and explicitly rejects Fragment (44). An implementer of the C or Rust codec reading the spec literally would walk into AH and diverge from the reference on AH-bearing packets — the exact interop divergence the profile exists to prevent. Fix: define the walked set normatively (e.g. 'the walk continues only through the TLV-style extension headers Hop-by-Hop (0), Routing (43), and Destination Options (60); every other Next Header value, including AH (51) and encapsulated IPv6 (41), terminates the walk as opaque payload, except Fragment (44) which is malformed'). Rust codec.rs and the C gate should be re-checked against the chosen wording.
close_reason: Re-close #4: TLV walk-set spec fix, 3x delegated review clean.
